dialogue.content: We are a couple in London. Can you fit out the flat from these photos?
Photographs can explain what you want to keep, but they cannot establish an accurate footprint. Please add a dimensioned plan, door positions and window measurements before we size the furniture.
Use this Swiss plan as a practice case. The advert says 900 square feet.
This reference contains 75.4 square metres of interior room area, with balconies excluded. An advertised figure may use another boundary, so I will not stretch the drawing to match it.
The largest unnamed room is our lounge and the others are bedrooms. Leave the walls alone.
I record those room uses as your decisions and preserve the source walls and openings. The lounge gives us 18.3 square metres for a sitting arrangement.
Choose a compact sofa and a low coffee table. Keep the existing kitchen and flooring.
For this test I choose a 1900 millimetre sofa and a 900 by 550 millimetre coffee table. Retaining the kitchen means its unmeasured cabinets are outside this furniture calculation.
A 140 centimetre mattress for us, singles in the other bedrooms, and 120 centimetre wardrobes.

The principal bedroom receives the 1400 millimetre mattress reference; the others receive 900 millimetre singles. The solver uses the compiled bed frames and the wardrobes, rather than treating mattress sizes as complete furniture footprints.
Does that prove the flat meets the English space standard?
No: England’s nationally described space standard is a planning standard whose applicability needs checking. Our net room sum is not its gross internal area, and ceiling height has not been measured.
Have you actually calculated the positions, including the doors?

The studio solver returned 6 placed pieces, and a separate geometric check examined their footprints and conservative door swing zones. The source retains 3 dimensional target exceptions instead of concealing them.
Keep that distinction in the handover; we have not measured our own flat yet.

The designer receives the reference plan, selected sizes and unresolved survey questions as a preliminary brief. They make the final design decision after checking your actual home and any applicable planning requirements.
